description: A secret-handling-policy artifact defines how every application secret is stored, rotated, scoped, and protected from inadvertent disclosure.

rules.description: The policy file must declare a project name so the policy can be traced to a specific system.
The secrets array must be present and contain at least one entry.
Each secret must declare: id, type, storage_backend, environments, max_age_days, rotation_required, log_safe, and allowed_consumers.
Production secrets must use a secrets manager (Vault, AWS SM, GCP SM) — plain environment variables are forbidden in production.
Every secret must have a max_age_days value greater than zero.
Secrets of type database_credential, signing_key, private_key, master_key, and root_credential must rotate within 90 days.
If rotation_required is false, a rotation_exemption_ref must reference an approved exception record.
log_safe must be explicitly false for every secret — plaintext logging of secret values is never acceptable.
Every secret must list at least one specific service identity in allowed_consumers.
Wildcard consumer values such as '*' or 'all' are forbidden — secrets must be scoped to named service identities.
When secret_path is declared per environment, staging and production paths must not be identical or share the same namespace prefix.
The policy file must not contain fields named value, default_value, or plaintext, and must not contain strings that pattern-match real credentials.
